title: Gameplay for my newest project Room For Ghosts
author: Wheelydope
selftext:
I'm building this tower defense style game called Room For Ghosts where you build a cozy village and soothe the lost spirits of the forest with things like warmth, music, food, housing, and light. 

Would love some feedback on the aesthetic, UI, and gameplay if anyone has the time! 

This is primarily made with Claude Opus 5.5 in UE5 while I give creative feedback and direction via playtesting. GPT Astra was used for polish, UI design, and some blender modeling.   
  
Music is made with Suno. Sound effects are mostly from the Gamemaster Audio Pro Sound Collection and a few procedural sounds.

comments.author: IceDry1780
comments.body: Wow, it turned out really well! How long did it take you? Do you plan to release it on Steam?

replies.author: Wheelydope
replies.body:
Thank you!! This took me about two weeks. Still have quite a few things to do before release on steam and hope to get some play testing feedback. It’s on itch.io if you’re interested in trying it! Would love some genuine feedback 

https://rainyporchgames.itch.io/room-for-ghosts

replies.author: IceDry1780
replies.body:
The idea is really good and innovative! Here's my feedback:

**What I liked:**

1. The day-to-night transition creates a really nice atmosphere.
2. The way the ghosts are presented reminds me a lot of those old-school games, not sure why, but I loved it.
3. I liked the house placement animations and the interactions in general. It all turned out really well, and I didn't run into any bugs.

**What I didn't like:**

1. I thought the tutorial was weak. Even though I never do tutorials myself, a game like this needs one that really walks players through things, for those who do like to read them.
2. The map felt a bit unfinished. I think you're already aware of this and planning to improve it, but the grass and fire have some movement when you zoom in close, while from far away everything looks static and lifeless. Not to mention that dragging the map to the side and seeing the edge of the world breaks the whole atmosphere.
3. The speed-up still feels slow. Even though it's a cozy game, I know some people will find the ghosts' walking pace slow even at 4x.
4. The game's UI is very raw and unfinished (but I think you already know that).
5. I found it hard to place the lanterns along the path to make it look nice the way I wanted. Cozy game players might get frustrated with that.

I only played for a few hours on my Windows PC, but I could already see the potential. Congrats!

replies.author: Wheelydope
replies.body:
This is great feedback and super helpful. 

I really appreciate you taking the time to test it out!

comments.author: drallcom3
comments.body:
The tech side looks pretty good.

What you need to do is to work more on the identity of the game. Are the ghosts good? Are they bad? What happens if they don't get what they want? How do I know what they want or will want next night? You also can't really react to them when they appear. You either fulfil their needs or you don't (also makes that phase rather boring).

comments.author: thetinytrex
comments.body: Like the cozy vibes! I really dig the concept. It seems to be original (at least I don't know of a cozy tower defense) which I really appreciate having seen so many clones of GTA these days.
